title: Followers of Horus secret societies preserving knowledge from the First Time
summary: Graham Hancock tells of Followers of Horus secret societies preserving knowledge from the First Time, about c. 10,500 BC to c. 3000 BC at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: that these were secret societies which were entrusted with preserving information from what they call the first time and passing it down to future generations.

plain: A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, drawing on his book Talisman written with Robert Bauval, says the Followers of Horus in ancient Egypt, named for the falcon-headed god, were secret societies. He says they were trusted to keep knowledge from what the Egyptians called the First Time, a distant early age, and pass it down the generations. If true, it would mean wisdom from a forgotten older civilisation survived through hidden groups.
